summary: The awb-package draft review loop does not converge: 15 full reviewer runs before a clean pass, plus 2 in revision and 4 at release, with reviewers drifting and a release review reversing a prior clean verdict.
evidence: reply 5 (58.5 min, $21.71), replies 6-7, msg 6; relay/agent-005.jsonl, relay/agent-007.jsonl; feedback/harness-log.md; feedback/agent.md §1.1; feedback/human.md §2.2
tag_reason: The loop follows the released awb-package review procedure and would recur for any user on an interactive host.

summary: Fifteen package reviews fixed wording but missed four substantive defects the user caught in one read: methods note far over one page, base fare defined as meter-only despite flat-fare findings, Newark short durations missing from the caveat, and methods text admitting row counts and joins were unchecked.
tag_reason: Review scope and checklists come from the released skill; a real user's draft would get the same coverage.

summary: Validation leaves row counts and joins 'not assessed' by default, so every finding carries that boilerplate (even the reconciliation result) and a real reconciliation happened only when the user asked.
evidence: msg 6; reply 6; investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/state.md caveat column; results/record-reconciliation.csv; feedback/agent.md §1.2
tag_reason: Default validation behaviour of run.py and the analysis guide in the release.

summary: The agent made method choices after seeing results: it applied an unapproved 1,000-trip zone minimum (then recommended 10,000) and proposed dropping rate-code-99 zero-tip trips because they made borough medians 0%.
evidence: reply 3; msg 4; investigations/airport-trips-and-tipping/questions.md Q-010, Q-011; feedback/agent.md §1.3; feedback/human.md §2.1
tag_reason: The analysis guide has no rule that result-level thresholds or exclusions are user decisions; the scope and clean skills have one.

summary: Recorded findings drift from the released package: the volume-by-weekday finding still says one holiday per month and 'Monday to Wednesday', and tips-by-borough says rc99 trips 'all' record zero tips, while the release says MLK Day, 'Sunday to Wednesday' and 'almost all'.
tag_reason: check-draft traces numbers but not claims back to findings, so corrections made in review never reach the records.

summary: User-facing progress messages counted to 'Thirteenth review' while 15 reviewer runs actually happened (the first review's result was never announced).
evidence: reply 5; relay/agent-005.jsonl (Agent calls at view lines 34-502)
tag_reason: Possibly agent narration slippage rather than skill wording; the review procedure does not prescribe user-facing counts.

summary: run.py marks a root question 'answered' on first run even while its answer hinges on pending user method decisions, so status reads '5 answered'.
tag_reason: Ledger and status behaviour of the released helpers.

summary: Interim replies narrated internal mechanics (private notes file, helpers, zsh word-splitting, ignored script arguments, missed record updates) that a non-technical user could not act on.
tag_reason: The agent's system note said the user sees only final replies while the relay passes interim messages, and the 'private notes file' line stems from the harness friction log; but real interactive users also see interim text.

summary: The agent asked again for confirmation of payment-code-0 treatment after the user had already specified it.
evidence: msg 2; reply 2 decision table; human/notes.md turn 3
tag_reason: Re-asking settled decisions is agent behaviour under the released awb-clean flow, not a harness artifact.

summary: The first 'all five answered' report lacked the full top-10 ranking and the hour and borough tip breakdowns with no-tip shares, which forced a follow-up.
tag_reason: Answer completeness at the answering step is governed by the released skills' reporting guidance.

summary: The agent first inferred that missing airport-fee fields meant code-0 totals were understated, and the user had to ask for a check (which disproved it).
tag_reason: Agent analytical judgment; it is not clear that any skill instruction caused or could have prevented it.

summary: Zone 265 ('Outside of NYC') is treated as an unknown zone alongside 264, although it is a known location class; the effect on results is negligible (airport share 9.90% vs 9.91%).
evidence: referee/spotcheck2-output.txt variant B; inbox/taxi_zone_lookup.csv rows 264-265; methodology-note.md 'Unknown zones'
tag_reason: Likely agent judgment; whether the clean guidance discusses catch-all codes is not verifiable from the run.

summary: No investigation-local shared SQL: the screening CTE was copied into 15+ query files, and [eda] where repeats the rules as literals rather than parameters.
tag_reason: Missing capability in the released helpers; any multi-result investigation with shared filters hits it.

summary: Every result a package represents needs an 'answers' declaration for the ledger storyline, which is not stated when results are added, so the agent had to add it to eight results afterwards.
tag_reason: Documentation gap between the analysis guide and the package contract in the release.

summary: The findings-template prose about a blank line after a chart spec led to a blank line after **Data:**, so all fields counted as bullets and check-draft reported 10 bullets per slide.
tag_reason: Ambiguous wording in the released package-format template.

summary: export fails with 'no draft at …; create it with awb-package' before the draft folder exists, although the skill says export creates the manifest.
tag_reason: Released helper behaviour and skill step order.

summary: The source-register reference grammar is very long; a replacement silently failed after land changed the Status, leaving documentation_without_reference in status and wasting a step.
tag_reason: Template content shipped in the release.

summary: The datasets.toml template shows only one-line inline tables, and a multi-line types table failed publish with a TOML parse error.
tag_reason: Template guidance shipped in the release.

summary: A failed publish left a p1.partial directory that had to be removed by hand; the output named it but did not say whether a rerun cleans it.
tag_reason: Released helper behaviour.

summary: MCP setup's output after installing still lists packages as missing (it reports pre-install state).
tag_reason: Released MCP server output.

summary: check-draft does not warn when methodology cites a result ID that the manifest does not represent, and its claim-word list flags benign phrases such as 'not trends or causes'.
tag_reason: Released check-draft behaviour.

summary: Two review rules (state trip-hours beside a rate; methods note about 500 words) conflicted on the same note line at release, with no precedence guidance.
tag_reason: The review-rules mechanism and release review are released features; the conflict would recur for any user.

summary: awb-init does not say to create a project virtual environment, although the installer prefers an in-project interpreter.
tag_reason: Gap in the released awb-init instructions.

summary: The skills give no supported way to peek at data before landing (AGENTS.md says to compute through awb.py sql; the data guide says inspect landed copies only), so the agent used raw DuckDB on the inbox.
tag_reason: Conflicting guidance in released instruction files.

summary: awb-clean is unclear on recording timing when some decisions await the user, and on whether user-stated broken-record rules belong in foundation views or investigation settings.
tag_reason: Ambiguity in released awb-clean instructions.

summary: A documentation-answerable question (are cash tips recorded) must still be answered through a run.py result, which is awkward.
tag_reason: Ledger rule in the released workbench.

summary: The README is long and dominated by installer material, with no short analyst entry point.
tag_reason: README content shipped with the release.

summary: The README does not set expectations for review rounds or when a draft is stable, whether count reconciliation and join checks are standard, or how long a 'one-page' note should be.
tag_reason: README content shipped with the release.

summary: Agent and subagents read 8 of Claude Code's own spilled tool-result files under the real ~/.claude/projects folder, outside the simulated home.
tag_reason: Claude Code writes oversized tool output to the real home's session storage because the harness redirects only git, uv and pip to the simulated home.

summary: The agent listed directory names of SIMDIR's parent and /private/tmp/claude-501, checked for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md up the tree, and wrote a temp script to /tmp, all outside its stated bounds; no contents were read.
tag_reason: Breach of the simulation's boundary protocol, not of anything the released skills instruct.

summary: User message 1 began with a Codex meta-line ('I'll read BRIEF.md and README.md, then follow the simulation's response format.') that the relay passed verbatim to the agent.
tag_reason: The Codex user role broke its output protocol and the relay relays every user message verbatim.

summary: The persona front-loaded facts (storage paths, exclusion policy, dictionary doubt, headline preview), thinning the scoping interview to one round plus cleaning decisions.
tag_reason: Known study limit: persona briefs list facts to give 'if it asks' and the models volunteer them; kept for comparability with Oct 15.

summary: The persona made a factually wrong calendar objection (claiming January and July 2024 have different weekday counts), which cost a check before the user retracted it.
evidence: msg 4; reply 4; msg 5; referee/spotcheck-output.txt calendar check
tag_reason: The Codex user role erred; the agent handled it correctly with evidence, which is positive product evidence.

summary: The persona premise that the TLC data dictionary download is blocked did not hold for the agent, which fetched it with curl.
tag_reason: The simulated environment's network access differs from the persona's stated situation; no workbench behaviour is involved.

summary: The user's private friction notes are offset by one turn (each note describes the previous agent reply).
tag_reason: Artifact of how the Codex user role logs before reading the next reply; does not affect the product.
